analysis: Examined three modified files. (1) coordinator/tests/api/billing/payouts/global_payouts_queue_test.go: test-only change. Head lines 57-69 set fake funding state to "processing" before the concurrent syncGlobalPayout calls and add a follow-up sync (head 66-69) asserting exactly one create and two quote calls (head 76-78). This strengthens the existing coverage that payout dispatch is idempotent, the funding key is persisted, and the ledger is not debited twice. It touches no production code, so it adds no attack surface. It relates to the payout and ledger assets (A-009, TB-008), but no threat IDs are directly affected. (2) docs/README.md and docs/architecture/README.md: documentation only, with stamp bumps and a new index entry for architecture/kv-cache-quantization.md. The index text claims that prefix-cache.md now covers 'compatible prefix reuse' and 'default-eligible encrypted SSD caching', and that kv-cache-quantization.md covers 'independent lossy checkpoint storage' and 'lossy native restore'. These are description-only changes in this PR. The canonical T-041 text says exact prefix reuse, with a 30-minute TTL. The linked kv-cache-quantization.md and any prefix-cache.md changes were not supplied. If the underlying code or docs actually introduce lossy or quantized SSD checkpoint restore, or non-exact compatible-prefix reuse, T-041/SEC-035 (cross-tenant and TTFT oracle, SSD at-rest posture) and the encryption.md and threat-model.yaml statements would need a refreshed sign-off. This PR does not itself show that behavior, so there is no finding. The next pass should check whether the companion kv-cache-quantization.md or Swift cache changes in the same PR alter KVCacheSSD semantics, salt scoping, or AAD.
